items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was a tenor saxophonist named Lefty Edwards who to me was another -- who epitomized the hard- bop approach.

ctx.x: If it could be said, who were the leaders on the Detroit scene at that point? I ran through my laundry list of musicians that I know of, of that period, or that could have been around, but who were the leaders? Who were teachers and leaders?

At a very young age Barry Harris was one of the teachers. There was a tenor saxophonist named Lefty Edwards who to me was another -- who epitomized the hard- bop approach. His lines were like Sonny Stitt’s lines. Sonny Stitt definitely, who was a native of Saganaw [Michigan]. That’s the Detroit area. He can definitely be considered one of the teachers and the leaders.
Was he on the scene while you were there?
